MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age: 75 years
Sex: Male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Specimen Type: EBUS biopsy
Clinical Diagnosis: Likely adenocarcinoma
Estimated Tumor Content: 100%
Reason for Testing: Suspected lung adenocarcinoma

TESTS PERFORMED
1. Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)
   - ALK rearrangement analysis
   - ROS1 rearrangement analysis

2. Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)
   - Targeted amplicon panel including EGFR, KRAS, NRAS, and BRAF genes

METHODOLOGY
FISH Analysis:
Dual-color break-apart probes were used to detect ALK and ROS1 gene rearrangements. A minimum of 50 tumor cell nuclei were evaluated for each probe set.

Molecular Analysis:
DNA was extracted from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue. Targeted amplicon sequencing was performed using next-generation sequencing technology. The assay has analytical sensitivity for detecting variants with allele frequency ≥2.5% when coverage is ≥100 reads.

RESULTS

FISH ANALYSIS:
ALK (2p23): NEGATIVE for rearrangement
- No ALK rearrangements detected in 50 cells examined
- 2-3 copies of ALK gene detected per cell
- Clinical significance of copy number variation unclear

ROS1 (6q22): NEGATIVE for rearrangement
- No ROS1 rearrangements detected in 50 cells examined

MOLECULAR ANALYSIS:
EGFR (NM_005228.5): Wild type
- No pathogenic variants detected
- NOTE: Low coverage for codons 854-875; variants in this region cannot be excluded

KRAS (NM_033360.4): Wild type
- No pathogenic variants detected

NRAS (NM_002524.5): Wild type
- No pathogenic variants detected

BRAF (NM_004333.6): Wild type
- No pathogenic variants detected

QUALITY METRICS:
- Average coverage depth: >500x for all genes except noted EGFR region
- Minimum coverage: ≥100 reads for variant calling

INTERPRETATION
No therapeutic or prognostic variants were detected in the analyzed genes. The absence of activating mutations in EGFR and the lack of ALK or ROS1 rearrangements suggest that this patient is unlikely to benefit from EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors based on the current genetic profile.

The presence of 2-3 copies of the ALK gene is of unclear clinical significance and may represent low-level amplification or aneuploidy.

LIMITATIONS
- This assay does not detect all possible genetic alterations
- Low coverage in EGFR codons 854-875 may result in false-negative results for variants in this region
- Results should be interpreted in conjunction with clinical and histopathological findings

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD
Reviewed by: [redacted name], MD
Report Date: [redacted date]
